I have farmed these 6.5 mu for 30 years. I never went to school, but I know this soil like my own hands. My son and his wife work in a factory in Handan, so they send some money home, but fertilizer is expensive this year — a bag of compound fertilizer is 150 yuan now, up from 130 last year. I still have to watch every yuan. I don't trust new ideas from outsiders. Last year, Old Li from the village committee told everyone to cut fertilizer, but his wheat was shorter than mine and he got less grain. I do what my neighbors do, and I do what worked last year. Last year my wheat got about 950 jin per mu and my maize got about 1100 jin per mu. This year I will do the same.

For wheat: In October I hire the rotary tiller for one day to prepare all 6.5 mu. I buy the improved wheat seed from Zhang's shop — the kind in the red and white bag, I don't read the name but Old Wang used it and his crop was good. I sow about 30 jin per mu. Before sowing, I spread one full 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the bag with three numbers, usually 15-15-15 or whatever the shop has. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I spread half a bag of urea per mu, about 20kg. I irrigate three times from my well: once after sowing if the rain doesn't come, once in spring, and once when the wheat starts heading. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and I spray one more time in April for bugs. I expect about 950 to 1000 jin per mu.

For maize: In June, as soon as the wheat is cut, I plant maize the same day — no time to till, the season is too short and every day matters. I buy hybrid maize seed, two big bags for my 6.5 mu. I put one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the planting holes with the seed — the high-nitrogen kind the shop sells for corn. I don't top dress maize, I never have, there is no time and the basal fertilizer is enough. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if it is dry, and once when the ears are getting big. I spray herbicide once, and I spray insecticide twice because the corn borers have been bad the last few years — better to spend the money than lose the ears. I expect about 1100 jin per mu.

I would rather spend a bit too much on fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I pay for safety.
